title: Personal Checking: Daily Interest Accrual and Cycle-End Crediting
content:
## Who earns interest

Only Personal Checking tiers that are interest-bearing earn interest. Dormant and restricted accounts on such tiers go on earning; charged-off and closed accounts do not.

## How a day's interest is worked out

Interest builds up day by day on the ledger balance at the close of every calendar day. That closing balance is the running total of every entry posted on or before the day; the days considered start the day after the prior cycle closed and end on the day the current cycle closes.

- A day ending at zero or below earns nothing.
- A day ending above zero earns at the APY attached to the top band floor of the tier's ladder that the balance reaches; that rate applies to the whole balance, not to slices of it.
- The day's interest is the balance multiplied by that APY expressed as a percentage, divided by 365.
- Each day is priced with whatever tier, and so whatever ladder, the account held on that particular day.

## Crediting

The daily amounts are added up without rounding across the statement cycle. Only the cycle total is rounded, half-up to the cent, and it is booked as a single interest credit dated the day the cycle closes. If the total rounds to 0.00, nothing is credited.

## Worked example (hypothetical ladder and balances)

A hypothetical ladder pays 0.04 percent from 0.00 USD and 0.08 percent from 15000.00 USD. In a 30-day cycle the account ends 20 days at 12000.00 USD and 10 days at 16000.00 USD.

- Each 12000.00 day: 12000.00 multiplied by 0.04 percent, divided by 365, is about 0.013151 USD.
- Each 16000.00 day reaches the 15000.00 floor, so the whole 16000.00 earns 0.08 percent: 16000.00 multiplied by 0.08 percent, divided by 365, is about 0.035068 USD.
- Cycle total before rounding: 20 days of the first plus 10 days of the second, about 0.263014 plus 0.350685, which is about 0.613699 USD; credited as 0.61 USD.
